questionText: How do you read custom properties from application.properties in your code?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can choose @Value for an isolated key or register a typed, validated @ConfigurationProperties object for a related group.

claims.statement: @Value supports placeholder resolution, conversion, and SpEL, while @ConfigurationProperties supports grouped typed binding, relaxed binding, and generated configuration metadata.
A @ConfigurationProperties type must be registered through configuration-properties scanning, @EnableConfigurationProperties, or ordinary Spring bean registration before it can be injected.
Spring Boot validates a bound configuration-properties type when it is annotated with @Validated and uses Jakarta Validation constraints, causing invalid configuration to fail during startup.

examples.title: Compile and test the exact typed payment configuration and banner injection

validation.command: Compile with Java 17 under Spring Boot 3.3.1, bind the exact payment.* values, assert their Java types, and assert startup failure for blank URL and negative retries
validation.expected: Duration and integer binding succeeds for valid values, @Value injects Orders, and invalid constrained values fail context startup

visuals.title: @Value and @ConfigurationProperties compared by binding shape and capability

notes: The learner Java block is Java 17 compatible; the fixture adds only a package and a test accessor around the exact shown declarations.

review.notes: Binding, conversion, relaxed-binding, metadata, registration, SpEL, and validation claims were checked against official Spring Boot, Spring Framework, and Jakarta Validation sources; positive and negative tests passed.
